name: Jesuitenkirche Innsbruck zur Heiligen Dreifaltigkeit
kurzbeschreibung: The Early Baroque Jesuit Church in Innsbruck: A monumental domed basilica housing the princely crypt of Archduke Leopold V and the mighty Schützenglocke.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Jesuit Church of the Holy Trinity (Universitätskirche) is located on Universitätsstraße in the historic university quarter of the Tyrolean provincial capital Innsbruck (Innsbruck region) at an altitude of approximately 574 meters. Constructed between 1627 and 1640 on the site of a predecessor collegiate church, this sanctuary ranks as an outstanding masterpiece of Early Baroque architecture in western Austria. Endowed by Archduke Leopold V and his art-loving consort Claudia de' Medici, the magnificent pilaster church with its prominent crossing dome was modeled after Rome's celebrated Jesuit mother church, Il Gesù. With its imposing twin towers and copper-clad dome, it shapes the historic skyline just moments from the Imperial Hofburg.

Dome, Princely Crypt & The Great Bell

The luminous, expansive nave of the Jesuit Church captivates with noble Baroque spatial harmony and masterful stucco ornamentation. The visual centerpiece is the majestic crossing dome, which floods the sanctuary with warm daylight. Beneath the presbytery lies the significant Leopoldine Princely Crypt: here rest the mortal remains of founders Archduke Leopold V, Claudia de' Medici, and their sons Ferdinand Karl and Sigismund Franz within ornate ceremonial sarcophagi. In a side chapel, world-renowned theologian Karl Rahner SJ found his final resting place. Another European landmark is the Schützenglocke hanging in the north tower: weighing 9,200 kilograms, it is the fourth-largest church bell in all of Austria, surpassed only by the Pummerin in Vienna's St. Stephen's Cathedral, the Boomerin in St. Florian, and the bell of Salzburg Cathedral. Its deep, solemn chime sounds on major liturgical feasts.

Visit & Getting There

The Jesuit Church in Innsbruck is open daily year-round from 08:00 to 19:00 (freely accessible outside of church services). Admission to explore the nave is free; donations for the preservation of this protected monument are gratefully received. Getting there: The church is situated at Universitätsstraße 8, directly opposite the Faculty of Theology and only a three-minute stroll from the Haus der Musik and the Hofburg. From Innsbruck Central Station, you can walk here in under ten minutes. The IVB transit stops Museumstraße and Polizeidirektion are located in the immediate vicinity. Motorists can make use of the nearby Citygarage or Landesmuseumsgarage parking garages.

Tips

The interior of the church is barrier-free and accessible for wheelchair users via both the main and side portals. Renowned for its superb acoustics and glorious Schuke pipe organ, the Jesuit Church regularly hosts solemn university masses, premier organ recitals, and sacred choral concerts. Pair your visit with a tranquil stroll through the neighboring imperial Hofgarten or a tour of the Tyrolean State Museums on Museumstraße.
